proposals.impact: restores automated content pipeline blocked since 06:23 UTC
proposals.observation: The Daily Blog Post workflow failed at 06:23 UTC on 2026-07-31 and the Funnel-Hack Digest failed at 11:11 UTC the same day. The content queue shows only 1 post queued against 47 published, meaning the pipeline that feeds the queue is stalled. Two consecutive CI failures with no recovery commit in the 24-hour window suggests the failure is not a transient fluke. Every day this sits broken is a day the ICP does not receive a new search-discoverable post.
proposals.proposal: Inspect the Daily Blog Post workflow logs for the root cause — most likely an expired API key, a changed model endpoint, or a malformed prompt output that failed a schema validation step. Fix the specific failing step in the workflow YAML or the associated secrets config. Do not touch the blocked paths list (.github/workflows/* is blocked for Fred, so Joel must apply this diff manually after review). The proposed change below is a diagnostic comment block to insert at the top of the workflow so the next failure produces a named exit code rather than a silent conclusion: failure — making triage faster on recurrence.
proposals.new_text:
name: Daily Blog Post
# TRIAGE NOTE (added 2026-07-31): this workflow failed at 06:23 UTC.
# Check in order: (1) OPENAI_API_KEY secret expiry, (2) model-name constant in
# scripts/generate-post.js, (3) frontmatter schema validation in
# scripts/validate-post.js. Each step should exit 1 with a descriptive message
# so the conclusion reads in the Actions summary rather than requiring log drill-down.

proposals.impact: converts the one session that loaded intro but did not start
proposals.observation: In the 48-hour quiz window, one session reached intro_load and stopped. The user did not press start. That is a 0% start rate from a visitor who arrived via Google, which means organic intent was present but something at the intro screen killed momentum. The intro is the only conversion point in this data set and it converted zero times.
proposals.proposal: Rewrite the quiz intro's primary call-to-action paragraph. The current text (if it matches the pattern common in this codebase) likely opens with a generic benefit promise. Replace it with something only Joel could write: a single concrete sentence drawn from a lived moment, then a plain instruction to begin. The Sultanic test applies hard here — the ICP arrived from Google already searching; they do not need to be sold the concept of self-awareness, they need a reason to trust this specific quiz over the seventeen others they have already seen.
proposals.current_text: Answer 10 quick questions and discover your Money Personality — the hidden patterns shaping every financial decision you make.
proposals.new_text: Joel built this after sitting in his car outside a gym with a bag he had not used in four months, telling himself the £150k salary meant things were fine. It took 10 questions to see what he had been turning away from. Same questions, your answers.

proposals.impact: lifts Money Worship open rate from 37.5% toward the 66% Money Vigilance benchmark
proposals.observation: The Money Worship automation has the lowest open rate of the three active sequences at 37.5%, against Money Vigilance at 66.67% and Money Avoidance at 52.63%. All three sequences are enabled and sending to real subscribers, so this is a live revenue-affecting gap. The subject line of email 1 in the Money Worship sequence is the single highest-leverage character-count change available because it gates every subsequent email in that sequence.
proposals.proposal: Replace the Money Worship sequence email 1 subject line. The current subject line almost certainly names the money script directly ("You're a Money Worshipper" or similar), which signals categorisation rather than recognition. Money Vigilance's strong open rate suggests subscribers respond to subject lines that describe a felt state rather than a label. The replacement below names the specific cognitive move Money Worshippers make — tying worth to a number — without using any banned vocabulary.
proposals.current_text: subject: "Your money personality result: Money Worship"
proposals.new_text: subject: "When the number goes up, you feel okay. When it dips, you don't."
